method: First900 pinned full-desktop sync source lines read; static comparison with already-reviewed Lite implementation.
findings: Full version declares Windows FFI to native scanner duplicate/search/delete operations; callsite limits, errors and free handling remain unread. Declarations are not runtime proof.

Issued-path set records canonical paths from search results and each returned duplicate file member. Validation requires absolute existing path and membership after canonicalization. This is path-session tracking, not content/identity/stamp snapshot; same-path mutation remains a separate lifecycle question.
Path key normalizes separators and ASCII case only. This is not universal Unicode casefold or filesystem object identity; actual Windows path aliases/case behavior unqualified.

DuplicateGroup carries full count/bytes separately from rendered files. Only returned file member paths are remembered; omitted capped members are not automatically issued in this helper. No claim remote action can target every group member.

Full/Lite implementations differ in trimming, pairing host-key parsing and generated transfer IDs; source duplication does not justify assuming identical behavior. No server/pairing action or credentials accessed.
Content MIME classification is extension-only and unknown becomes octet-stream; destination categories use supplied content_type. Neither indicates decoder verification or byte-content identity.
Filename sanitizer and free-path scan follow same general mechanism as Lite, but this full-version creation callsite is still unread; Lite create_new qualification must not be silently transferred.
No local dedup production change justified from these transport wrappers alone. Native scanner algorithm already reviewed separately remains the content-comparison reference.
